newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - July 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - July 4.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

In a move that will be seen as a vote of no confidence in one of Australia's most important exports, the Reserve Bank of Australia has sold two thirds of its gold reserves at an average price of US$350 a tonne for a total profit of A$2.1 billion. Treasurer Peter Costello commented on the sale by saying gold no longer has international financial significance. Page 1.

The Federal Government's new non-union employment contracts - the Australian Workplace Agreements - are being well received by Australian business as they are used to strip away penalty rates, free up working hours, and demolish union-enforced work practies and demarcations. Page 1.

The skilled vacancy survey compiled by the Department of Employment, Education, Training and Youth Affairs dropped 0.7 per cent in June, continuing a decline from the beginning of the year. The figure indicates a flat market and an uphill battle for the Federal Government if it is to meet its jobs growth targets. Page 3.

Manpower Services Australia managing director Malcolm Jackman said yesterday the Federal Government's Public Employment Placement Enterprise (PEPE) may not be worth his organisation's involvement after legislation providing for it was dropped by the Goverment because of Senate problems. Page 5.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Mining giant Rio Tinto, formerly known as RTZ-CRA, will today use non-union labour in an attempt to break a union picket line at its Hunter Valley No. 1 mine. Coal will be loaded on to a train at the mine by management staff, some white-collar workers and seven miners who have volunteered to sign individual work contracts. Page 1.

The Reserve Bank's decision to sell off 167 tonnes of its 247 tonne storage of gold in return for government securities indicates that gold is no longer considered a sound low-inflation investment. The sell-off should reap good profits for the bank as the gold was delivering no such gains. Page 1.

Mercantile Mutual has formally objected to the construction of a mobile phone tower by Vodafone on one of its properties because of the dangers of electromagnetic emission and its potential liability. In a move that is expected to ignite the debate over the health risks of mobile phone towers, Mercantile Mutual said scientific and medical evidence increasingly pointed to the health risks "posed by exposure to emissions from telecommunications base stations." Page 3.

Tasmanian poet Peter Shoobridge was granted his last wish yesterday when he and his four daughters whom he brutally murdered on the weekend before killing himself were laid to rest together at St Luke's Anglican Church in Richmond, just 10 kilometres from the murder scene. Page 3.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Following a landmark meeting between Federal Treasurer Peter Costello and Australia's leading welfare lobby group the Australian Council of Social Service, the Federal Government has confirmed it is willing to look into broadening income tax bases, includng a tightening on family trusts. Page 1.

The Reserve Bank is left with just over 80 tonnes of gold after selling 167 tonnes for A$2.4 billion. The decision to sell does not augur well for Australia, which is rich in gold resources, and reflects a fundamental change of thinking about the need to hold big gold reserves. Page 1.

The New South Wales Legal Services Tribunal struck Aboriginal lawyer and activist Paul Coe off the roll of legal practitioners yesterday after he was found guilty of professional misconduct. After the Tribunal said Coe was not a "fit and proper person to remain on the roll", Coe said he would appeal, and that it confirmed his view that it is still "a white man's world". Page 3.

Police announced yesterday that the search in bushland around Goulburn for clues relating to the kidnapping of Kerry Whelan from Sydney has been called off after police were unable to find anything to assist their inquires. Mrs Whelan vanished from Parraatta more than eight weeks ago. Page 3.
THE AGE

Supreme Court judge Justice Frank Vincent has urged the Victorian Government to establish an independent body to monitor the behaviour of State politicians after being unable to rule on the case against Liberal MP Bruce Atkinson. Victorian Premier Jeff Knnett said the Government will respond to the recommendation. Page 1.

In a statement issued by the Treasury last night, it was revealed that the Reserve Bank has been selling two-thirds of Australia's official gold reserves over the past six months. In return the RBA has bought United States, Japanese, German and other govrnment securities. Page 1.

English actor Rowan Atkinson was in Australia yesterday to promote the new film starring his famous character Mr Bean. Atkinson's English accent and sophistication assisted him in pointing out the differences between himself and his character, a day after the film Bean had its world premiere in Sydney. Page 1.

A book written by Australian Financial Review associate editor Pamela Williams says Kerry Packer's son James considered entering Federal politics last year as the Liberal member for Kooyong, and was dissuaded by his father because his political ambitions would clash with the family's wish to own the John Fairfax newspaper empire. Page 3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
